title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Overview: what a compiler is
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. A compiler translates source text into an executable form through stages: lexing (characters to tokens), parsing (tokens to a syntax tree), code generation (tree to instructions), and execution (instructions to a result). A toolchain chains these stages with preprocessing, optimization, assembly, and linking. This database carries REAL implementations of every stage — not descriptions of compilers, but compilers. Every demo below executes the actual code. Note: a companion toolchain database (advdb-compiler-language-toolchain) covers toolchain organization; this database is the runnable-implementation companion, and the per-language compiler databases (MiniC, MiniC#, MiniJava, MiniRust, MiniGo) carry the individual language front ends.

title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Stage 1: the lexer
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. The lexer scans raw characters and emits tokens: numbers, operators, parentheses. It rejects bad characters immediately with a precise error rather than failing mysteriously later. The implementation below is a hand-written scanner — no generator tools, no dependencies — so its behavior is fully visible. The demo tokenizes an expression and asserts the token stream.

title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Stage 2: the parser
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. The parser is a recursive-descent implementation with correct operator precedence: unary minus binds tightest, then multiplication/division/modulo, then addition/subtraction, with parentheses overriding. It builds an abstract syntax tree and rejects trailing garbage and malformed input. The demo parses an expression and asserts the tree shape.

title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Stage 3: code generation
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. Code generation walks the syntax tree and emits stack-machine bytecode: push constants, apply operators, negate. The instruction set is tiny (push, neg, +, -, *, /, %) and completely specified, so the generated code can be inspected, tested, and reasoned about. The demo compiles an expression and asserts the exact instruction sequence.

title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Stage 4: the virtual machine
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. The virtual machine executes bytecode on an operand stack: push puts values on, operators pop two and push the result, neg flips the top. Integer division truncates toward negative infinity consistently. The demo runs compiled bytecode and asserts the computed value, proving the whole pipeline computes correctly.

title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Language front ends
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. Front ends adapt the core compiler to language-shaped syntax: MiniC (int main), MiniC# (static int Main), MiniJava (static int run), MiniRust (fn main -> i32), MiniGo (func main() int). Each front end extracts the expression body with its own grammar rule and shares the verified backend. The demo runs the same computation through two different front ends and asserts identical results — proving the backend is language-independent.

title: The Signature Compiler Implementations and Toolchains Database — Tests and verification
body: Signature edition. Original Signature compiler methods and framings, labeled Signature throughout. Verification: the pipeline is tested on precedence, parentheses, unary minus, integer division, modulo, error rejection, and cross-front-end consistency. Every test executes at build time; the verified outputs are recorded in each demo. Limits: this is an expression compiler, not a full language — no variables, functions, or control flow. Those are the honest boundaries of this implementation; the generator ladder extends toward them.
